title: Shadow Experiments Console flow: create experiment, select variants, view deltas, drill into examples
creator: Kenji Nakamura
project: Shadow traffic tool for eval metrics
description:
Objective
Design the end-to-end Console UX flow for Shadow Experiments: (1) create an experiment, (2) select control vs one or more shadow variants, (3) review quality deltas alongside latency/cost/error metrics, and (4) drill into sampled examples for debugging. This ticket covers wireframes + interaction notes suitable for engineering implementation (ENG-5408) and API shaping feedback (ENG-5407).

Background / user problem
Customers are comfortable canarying for latency/cost, but hesitate to roll out new models/quantization/routing policies without measuring quality regressions. Shadow traffic mirrors a sampled subset of live requests to candidate variants while returning the control response to the end user. Console needs to make this understandable, safe, and interpretable (especially around statistical confidence, sampling, and data retention).

Primary personas
1) ML Engineer (quality owner): wants confidence that candidate is not worse; needs example-level debug.
2) Platform Engineer (routing owner): wants to attach a shadow experiment to a route/rollout safely; needs clear guardrails + cost/overhead visibility.

Entry points (proposed)
A) Route details → “Quality” tab → “Run shadow experiment” CTA
- Preselects route + current active model/version as Control.
- Best for day-to-day “should we change the route?” workflows.

B) Rollout (canary/A-B) timeline → “Attach shadow experiment”
- Adds quality signals to rollout context.
- Requires mapping to rollout variants and clear “advisory only” messaging in v1.

C) Experiments index → “Create shadow experiment”
- For power users and auditors; includes full list of experiments across routes.

Navigation placement
- Left nav: Observability → Quality (new) OR Rollouts → Quality signals (TBD). For beta, ship as a subpage under Rollouts to reduce IA churn.

Flow 1: Create Shadow Experiment (wizard)
Step 0: Choose scope
- Fields:
  - Name (required)
  - Route (required)
  - Environment: Prod | Staging (if customer has both; internal tenants only for now)
  - Start: “Start now” vs schedule (schedule is out of scope; show as disabled w/ tooltip “coming soon”)
- Notes:
  - Route picker should show current model, region, and whether streaming is enabled.
  - Add a callout if route is streaming: “Streaming requests are shadowed with partial capture rules; example previews may be truncated.” (Align with ENG-5414).

Step 1: Traffic sampling & safety
- Fields:
  - Sampling rate (default 1%; allowed range 0.1%–10% depending on plan; show enforcement hint “Max sampling depends on quota/plan”)
  - Bucketing: “Sticky” (recommended) vs “Random” (advanced)
    - Sticky = deterministic fingerprinting so the same user/request pattern stays in bucket across time windows.
  - Shadow timeout (advanced; default hidden): e.g., 1500ms; “Shadow path is fail-open; user response unaffected.”
- Guardrails UI:
  - Non-blocking warning: “Shadowing increases GPU usage and telemetry. Start at 0.5–1% and scale once scoring lag is stable.”
  - Show estimated incremental cost range (if available) or placeholder: “Cost estimate available after first 15 minutes of data.”

Step 2: Select variants
- Control (locked)
  - Control target is current production response for the route (the user-visible response).
  - Show pinned identifiers: model_id, model_version, quantization profile, routing policy version.
- Shadow variants (1–3 in beta)
  - “Add variant” button
  - Variant types (radio):
    1) Model version (same family)
    2) Quantization profile
    3) Routing policy (e.g., different region / capacity tier)
    4) Prompt template (if route has templating enabled)
  - For each variant, show:
    - Display name (user-editable)
    - Target details (read-only summary)
    - Expected compatibility warnings (e.g., “Candidate model does not support tool calling; responses may differ”) if we have metadata.
- Constraints / validation (UX):
  - Disallow multiple changes per variant by default (reduce ambiguity). Provide “Advanced: allow multi-change variant” behind a toggle; likely disabled for beta.
  - If a variant changes output schema (e.g., structured output), show blocking warning: “Format adherence metrics required” and preselect them.

Step 3: Choose quality metric bundle
- Default: “Quality bundle v1 (recommended)”
  - Includes: format adherence, refusal/safety, instruction following, “helpfulness proxy” rubric score.
- Advanced: “Customize metrics” (accordion)
  - Allow enabling/disabling specific metrics. If disabled, warn: “You may miss regressions in {category}.”
  - Show rubric version pinning (read-only for beta): “Rubric version: 1.0.0 (pinned per experiment)”
- Important UI copy: “These scores are computed asynchronously and may lag by several minutes.”

Step 4: Data handling & retention
- Always show this step in beta; designed to reduce surprises.
- Fields:
  - Prompt/response retention: default “24 hours (recommended)” with dropdown (Dedicated may allow 7d/30d; Hosted likely fixed short)
  - Redaction: “Default Redwood redaction” (on) + “Add fields to redact” (text input; only for customers w/ advanced plan; may be hidden)
  - Example storage: “Store up to N scored examples” (defaults aligned w/ cardinality guardrails)
- Copy:
  - “Shadow artifacts may contain sensitive data. Ensure retention aligns with your policies.”

Step 5: Review & launch
- Summary card:
  - Route, sampling, control target, variants list, metric bundle, retention
- “Launch experiment” primary button
- Secondary: “Save as draft” (supported; drafts don’t enable shadowing)
- Post-launch toast + deep link to results page.

Flow 2: Results overview (per experiment)
Top header
- Experiment name + status pill: Draft | Running | Paused | Completed
- Controls:
  - Time range: last 15m / 1h / 24h / custom
  - Segment filter (beta limited): region, request_type (chat vs completions), streaming (yes/no), route version (if relevant)
  - “Pause” and “Stop” actions (Stop is destructive; confirm modal)

Tabs
1) Summary (default)
- “Is it worse?” callout
  - For each variant: show headline delta for primary score (e.g., rubric score) + confidence indicator.
  - Suggested states:
    - Green: “No regression detected (95% CI)”
    - Yellow: “Inconclusive (insufficient samples / high variance)”
    - Red: “Regression detected”
- Quality deltas chart
  - X-axis: time; Y-axis: delta vs control
  - Show confidence band (shaded) and sample size overlay on hover.
- Supporting metrics row
  - Refusal rate delta
  - Format adherence delta
  - Instruction-following delta
  - Scoring lag (p50/p95) + “latest scored at {timestamp}”
- Operational metrics row (for sanity)
  - Shadow target error rate
  - Shadow timeouts
  - Incremental token/cost estimate
  - Overhead: extra compute (if available) or “N/A”

2) Metrics detail
- Table: Metric × Variant
  - Columns: Control, Variant A, Δ, CI, n (samples), last updated
  - Sorting: by worst regression / largest magnitude
  - Inline tooltips describing each metric and common failure modes.

3) Examples
- Purpose: enable debugging without drowning users.
- List view with filters:
  - Filter by metric outcome (e.g., “format failures”, “refusals”, “largest negative delta”, “largest disagreement”)
  - Search (by request_id if user has it)
- Row contents:
  - Timestamp
  - Request fingerprint (hashed)
  - Score summary badges (e.g., Format: Fail; Safety: Pass)
  - “View comparison” CTA
- Example detail drawer
  - Three-column layout:
    - Input (redacted/truncated) with “show more” gated by permissions
    - Control output
    - Variant output
  - Score breakdown + evaluator notes (model-graded rubric rationale, if we store it)
  - Action buttons:
    - “Copy as eval-harness case” (exports JSON snippet)
    - “Mark as known issue” (writes a note; v1 could be local-only annotation)

Flow 3: Attach to Rollout (quality signals)
- Rollout page: new side panel “Quality (Shadow)” with:
  - Link to the attached experiment
  - Current status (scoring lag, sample size)
  - Headline delta states (green/yellow/red)
- Important v1 constraint: quality signals are advisory; do not auto-rollback.
  - Copy: “Quality signals do not automatically change traffic allocation in this release.”

Permissions / RBAC notes
- “Create experiment” requires: Rollouts:Write + Observability:Write (naming TBD).
- “View examples” requires elevated permission due to potential sensitive prompt content.
  - Non-privileged users see aggregate charts but example drawer shows “You don’t have permission to view raw prompts/outputs.”

Empty/error states (must design)
- Running but no scored data yet
  - Show skeleton + message: “Collecting samples. First results typically appear within 5–10 minutes.”
- Scoring lagging/backlog
  - Banner: “Scoring is delayed (p95 lag 28m). Metrics may be stale.” + link to status/runbook for internal tenants.
- Shadow path degraded
  - Banner: “Shadow targets are timing out. Experiment is still running, but coverage is reduced.”
- Inconclusive / insufficient power
  - State: “Not enough samples to draw conclusions.” Provide suggested sampling increase and expected time to power (if we have it; otherwise simple guidance).

Key wireframe decisions made in this ticket
- Wizard-based creation to force safety/retention acknowledgement before enabling shadowing.
- Results page prioritizes a single “Is it worse?” callout to reduce misreads of noisy charts.
- Examples are behind a dedicated tab + strict permission gating.
- Confidence intervals are displayed by default (not an advanced toggle) to set expectations.

Open questions (needs product/eng alignment)
1) Variant limit for beta: 1 vs 3. Design supports 3 but UX is cleaner at 1; recommend 1 default + allow “Add variant” for internal/beta.
2) Segment filters: which dimensions are safe for cardinality? Proposed minimum: region + request_type only.
3) Retention UI for Hosted: if fixed, should we hide dropdown and show a static callout? (Probably yes.)
4) How to represent “sticky bucketing” in customer-friendly terms without exposing fingerprinting details.
5) Export format for “Copy as eval-harness case”: align with Applied ML (Jonas/Karthik) on schema.

Collaboration / reviews
- Reviewed with Marissa Cole (PM, Console & Rollouts) on 2026-02-06: requested stronger upfront cost/overhead messaging and clearer advisory-only language on rollouts.
- Eng sync with Dylan Brooks + Chloe Martin on 2026-02-07: confirmed wizard steps map to planned API objects; requested explicit handling for Draft vs Running states.
- Applied ML input from Selene Huang on 2026-02-08: confidence display is mandatory; add “inconclusive” state and sample size surfacing.

Deliverables
- Wireframes (Figma): Create wizard (steps 0–5), Results (Summary/Metrics/Examples), Rollout attachment panel.
- UI copy draft for warnings/tooltips (handoff to DES-613 for finalization).
- Implementation notes for ENG-5408 (component breakdown: header controls, delta charts, examples drawer).

Acceptance criteria
- Engineer can implement create flow without ambiguous state transitions (Draft → Running → Paused/Stopped).
- Results page clearly communicates: delta magnitude, direction, confidence, and sample size.
- Examples drilldown supports side-by-side comparison and is permission-gated.
- Error/empty states are defined for: no data, lagging scoring, degraded shadow target.
